But the method's public signature takes an optional Express `Request` parameter (`request?: Request`). That ties the use case's input boundary to the HTTP framework. Handling HTTP requests belongs to the transport layer (here, infrastructure/http routes). The parameter is unused, so no transport logic runs, but the HTTP coupling is still part of the use case's contract. That is a misplaced framework responsibility rather than just an import-direction issue. Confidence is moderate because the violation is in the signature, not in behaviour.
